3.q: אָמַ֨רְתָּ֙ אֽוֹי־נָ֣א לִ֔⁠י כִּֽי־יָסַ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה יָג֖וֹן עַל־מַכְאֹבִ֑⁠י יָגַ֨עְתִּי֙ בְּ⁠אַנְחָתִ֔⁠י וּ⁠מְנוּחָ֖ה לֹ֥א מָצָֽאתִי
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [You have said that it is terrible for you now, because Yahweh has added sorrow to your pain, and that you are weary with your groaning and have not found rest.]
See how you translated this phrase in 4:31.

Baruch is speaking as if **sorrow** were a burden that Yahweh had **added** on top of the **pain** that Baruch was already carrying. He means that Yahweh has caused him to experience sorrow in addition to the pain he was already suffering. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has made me sorrowful in addition to the pain that I already have]

Baruch is speaking as if **rest** were an object that a person could look for and find. He means that he has not been able to rest. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I have not been able to rest]

4.q: כֹּ֣ה תֹּאמַ֣ר אֵלָ֗י⁠ו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה
4.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Thus you shall give him this message from me, Yahweh]

Yahweh is speaking as if his people were a building that he had **built** and that he is now **tearing down**. He means that he established the people of Judah as a nation and is now destroying that nation. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the nation that I established, I am destroying]

Yahweh is speaking as if his people were a plant that he had **planted** and that he is now **plucking up**. He means that he settled his people in their land and is now removing them from it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people whom I have settled in their land, I am removing from it]

4.q: and this with regard to all of the earth
4.note: The phrase **all of the earth** could refer to: (1) the entire earth. Alternate translation: [and I will do this to the entire world] or [and I will do this to the entire earth] (2) all the land of Judah. Alternate translation: [and I will do this to all of the land of Judah]
The pronoun **you** refers to Jeremiah, and the pronoun **him** refers to Baruch. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [you, Jeremiah, shall say to Baruch]
See how you translated the similar expression in 15:10.

5.note: It might seem that the expression **where you will go there** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [where you will go]

5.q: And you, do you seek great things for yourself?
5.note: Yahweh uses a question to show Baruch his astonishment that Baruch is hoping or seeking for great things in a community that God is about to bring disaster on. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation as in the UST.

5.q: your life will be to you for spoil
5.note: See how you translated the similar phrase in Jeremiah 21:9
Bible scholars are not certain what the **great things** are that Yahweh is telling Baruch not to **seek** so in your translation it is best to not explain what the those things might be.

The word **For** indicates that what follows is the reason why Baruch should not seek great things for himself. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]
